newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX power ends up on cash, San Onofre concerns.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX power ends up on cash, San Onofre concerns.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled higher Thursday on strength in the western physical power market and concerns over one of the San Onofre Nuclear Generating Station (SONGS) units in California.
Brokers and traders said the futures market was worried SONGS unit 3 would not contribute power to the grid today as scheduled earlier.
"There's some apprehension that these units won't come back on line," a West Coast broker said, referring to SONGS units 2 and 3.
The 1,080 megawatt (MW) SONGS unit 3 remained off line, while engineers have been correcting a water contamination problem in the unit's lube oil system, the operator said.
Southern California Edison earlier said it expected to know later today whether the unit would resume ramping up to power by tonight.
The adjacent 1,070 MW unit 2 was holding at 70 percent power while maintenance work on a main feedwater pump is being carried out.
August Palo Verde (PV) futures settled up $2.01 at $36.68 a megawatt hour (MWh) after posting a high at $36.75.
September PV finished up 82 cents at $29.20. Deferred PV ended 15 to 30 cents higher.
August California Oregon Border (COB) settled up 42 cents at $22.04 a MWh after hitting a session high at $22.30.
September COB finish up 32 cents at $22.13. Other COB months ended five to 15 cents higher.
"The cash market is extremely strong," said a Houston futures trader.
Amid extreme heat in parts of the Southwest, next-day peak power prices at PV jumped five dollars to $49.00-52.00 a MWh, whiie those at COB firmed 25 cents to $17.25-18.25.
Forecasters called for normal temperatures to continue across the Pacific Northwest into next week, and hot but seasonal weather over most of the Southwest.
Amid expectations of cash market prices continuing their rise Friday, brokers and traders said the market will focus on any updates about the operating status of the SONGS units.
In other generation news, output at the 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear power plant in Richland, Washington, achieved 87 percent early Thursday.

The 750 MW Mohave coal-fired unit 3 was shut Monday for repairs and expected to resume operations Saturday, while the 550 MW unit 3 at the Jim Bridger coal-fired complex in Wyoming may restart later today.
The 254 MW Valmy coal-fired unit 1 in Nevada was unlikely to return to full power until the weekend, after its output was halved Tuesday because of a tube leak.
Separately, southbound capacity on the AC segment of the Pacific Intertie transmission system was set to be cut by 250 MW to 3,200 MW between 0900 and 1600 PDT today and Friday for maintenance work.
